questions.note: Hallux longest, toe 2 a few mm shorter, a knuckle and a pulp on each: the plan is right. But both joints wear one stamp of parallel grooves, toe 2's DIP crease is a knife cut, its distal segment is finger-long and from below its end reads as a fitted cap, and the hallux rises from the ball with no sulcus.

Both plates have edge thickness and a fold rim, are trimmed straight and neither floats nor sinks, but they read as press-on acrylic: flat even-pink tiles in an even gutter, a constant-width grey-cream French-tip edge under a red outline, no lunula, an S-kinked medial border, a near-white combed sheen and a carved pocket under the free edge.

Nothing in scope reads as tendon relief: no EHL cord over the first MTP onto the hallux and no extensor slip to toe 2; the dorsum is smooth generic skin, and the only linear relief there is a scar-like glossy arc across the MTP. No veins show either.

Shadow sides stay dark and nothing glows, but the micro-relief gives it away: a crumpled-cellophane crackle that glints on the dorsum, one straight diagonal hatching for the ridges on every plantar surface, and soft featureless patches beside crisp ones in the zooms. Colour is left aside as the declared first pass.

defects.what: The hallux nail is a flat, evenly pink, unridged tile seated in a constant-width gutter with one thin raised rim on three sides, every edge exposed: a press-on, not a plate that grows from under the proximal fold and sinks under fleshy lateral folds.
defects.fix: A real plate emerges from under a thin cuticle, its sides sink under lateral folds that deepen toward the root, it arches transversely and shows faint longitudinal ridges and uneven pink-to-ivory colour.

defects.what: Both free edges still read as a French manicure: on the hallux a constant-width grey-cream strip under a wavy pale line and a thin red outline, on toe 2 a crisp white line; a man's trimmed edge is ivory to yellowish, uneven in width and slightly ragged.
defects.fix: A real free edge is the same plate seen without its bed: its width varies along the cut, a soft 0.5–1 mm onychodermal band precedes it instead of an outline, faint grime lies beneath, the trim is slightly irregular.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wear one stamp: three or four long, evenly spaced, parallel glossy grooves spanning the joint, which also notch the dorsal profile like bellows in the medial view.
defects.fix: Knuckle skin crinkles in short, broken, uneven folds that fork, fade at the sides and differ from toe to toe, over a slightly darker, rougher patch on the joint.

defects.what: The hallux tuft is about ten straight, stiff, equally dark strokes splayed both ways in a symmetric chevron, with no taper, curl or contact shadow: ink scratches rather than hair. Toe 2 has one tiny forked stroke.
defects.fix: Real tuft hairs lie flat, combed distally and a little laterally with 10–20° scatter, each curved and tapered, varying in length and darkness, shading the skin; toe 2 carries two to four fine hairs.

defects.what: The plantar ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle over the ball, both pulps and the phalanges, running unbroken across the flexion creases: a hatching texture.
defects.fix: Friction ridges form a whorl or loop on each pulp, run roughly transverse on the phalanges and the ball, and break and turn at every crease.

defects.what: From below a crisp seam rings toe 2 at the PIP and the outline steps in under it, so the toe's end reads as a cap fitted on, like the old toes 3–4 beside it.
defects.fix: A plantar PIP crease is a soft fold within continuous skin; the outline narrows smoothly across it.

defects.what: The 1–2 web ends in a straight, level margin, a flat shelf strung between the hallux and toe 2; the same straight edge shows in the front and clay views.
defects.fix: A web margin is a soft U, deepest midway between the toes, its skin rolling under smoothly into the plantar side.

defects.what: No EHL cord runs over the first MTP onto the hallux and no extensor slip to toe 2: the dorsum over both toes is smooth, generic skin with no tendon relief.
defects.fix: A lean 40-year-old's forefoot shows the EHL as a firm ridge running onto the hallux and the long extensor to toe 2 as a softer one, both catching the light.

defects.what: About 8 mm of bare skin lies between toe 2's DIP crease and its nail fold, so the distal segment reads finger-long.
defects.fix: On a second toe the nail fold starts a few millimetres past the DIP crease; the distal segment is short and stubby, mostly nail and pulp.

defects.what: The dorsal micro-relief is one crackle of sharp crumpled-cellophane facets that glitter wherever a highlight crosses them, the same on toe 2's shaft, its knuckle and the web; visible at native size in the toe 2 closeup.
defects.fix: Real dorsal skin has finer, softer cells of 0.25–0.6 mm with rounded valleys and follicle pits, varying by region, so its sheen breaks up softly instead of glinting off facets.

defects.what: A single thin raised glossy arc crosses the first MTP dorsum and notches the dorsal profile in the medial view: it reads as a healed surgical scar.
defects.fix: MTP dorsal skin shows a few fine, short, broken transverse wrinkles, matte and shallow, fading out at the sides.

defects.what: Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even groove across two-thirds of the toe, a knife cut.
defects.fix: Two or three short, soft, broken creases with a slight roll of skin between them, fading before the sides.

defects.what: From below the hallux grows straight out of the ball with no toe-base sulcus and only a faint IP crease, its medial side one straight line from ball to pulp.
defects.fix: A deep curved crease sets the hallux off from the ball pad; the proximal pad and the pulp each bulge, split by a clear IP flexion crease.

defects.what: The hallux has no lunula: the plate is one even pink right up to the proximal fold, with no pale half-moon and no depth to the bed, which adds to the painted-tile look.
defects.fix: A dull, slightly milky half-moon about 3.5 mm deep, centred, its convex distal edge soft and partly hidden under the fold.

defects.what: The medial border of the hallux nail bends in an S halfway down where the fold pinches inward, leaving a crisp kinked gutter that reads as a mesh fault.
defects.fix: A real side edge is a smooth, gently convex arc, and the fold follows it with an even soft roll that deepens toward the root.

defects.what: The hallux plate goes near-white with soft vertical combing, like polished acrylic.
defects.fix: Keratin over the bed stays pink and translucent, with a smaller, softer sheen broken by faint longitudinal ridges.

defects.what: The free edge is an opaque grey-green strip of constant width with fine vertical striations, split from the plate by a thin red outline, its rounded corner melting into the fold skin: a laminated tape.
defects.fix: A real free edge is ivory and slightly translucent at the cut, varies in width, has a soft onychodermal band behind it and a small dark gap under its corner.

defects.what: Below the hallux free edge the pulp and hyponychium are soft and featureless while the side wall beside them, at the same depth, carries a crisp crackle: detail sharp in one place and blurred in the next.
defects.fix: Real skin keeps one consistent micro-relief across pulp, hyponychium and side wall: fine ridges on the pulp, finer cells on the sides, at the same sharpness.

defects.what: The shadowed recess of the web breaks into soft blotches with no micro-relief, like denoiser smear, so the web skin goes waxy.
defects.fix: Real web skin keeps its fine lines and cells into the shadow, only at lower contrast.

defects.what: In clay the hallux free edge sits over a crescent pocket with a rim concentric with the edge, as if the plate were seated in a carved cup.
defects.fix: The hyponychium meets the plate's underside in a shallow, soft groove that follows the pulp, not the free edge.

defects.what: From below the hallux's nail corners and the line of its free edge show past the pulp as dark slivers, and toe 2's tip ends in a crumpled outline with a dark nail sliver.
defects.fix: A big toe's pulp reaches past its nail and hides it from below; the end of each pulp is a smooth dome.

ranked: [D1] The hallux nail, the focus of three views, is a press-on: a flat, evenly pink, unridged tile in a constant-width gutter with one thin rim on three sides, every edge exposed. A real plate emerges from under a cuticle and sinks under soft lateral folds.

[D2] Both free edges are still a French manicure: a constant-width grey-cream strip under a wavy line and a thin red outline on the hallux, a crisp white line on toe 2. A man's trimmed edge is ivory to yellowish, uneven in width, a little ragged, with grime beneath.

[D3] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP carry the same stamp of three or four long, evenly spaced, glossy parallel grooves, notching the profile like bellows in the medial view. Real knuckle skin crinkles in short, broken, uneven folds that differ toe to toe.

[D4] The new hallux tuft reads as ink scratches: about ten straight, stiff, equally dark strokes splayed both ways in a symmetric chevron, with no taper, curl or shadow. Real tuft hairs curve, taper and lie flat toward the tip; toe 2 has only one forked stroke.

[D5] From below every plantar surface wears the same straight diagonal hatching, ball, pulps and phalanges alike, running across the creases; real ridges whorl or loop on each pulp and break at every crease. At native size it reads as a procedural stripe.
[D6] From below a crisp seam still rings toe 2 at the PIP and its outline steps in under it, so the end of the toe reads as a cap fitted on, exactly like the old toes 3–4 beside it.
[D7] The 1–2 web still ends in a straight, level margin, a flat shelf between the toes in the front, closeup and clay views; a real web margin is a soft U, deepest midway, rolling under to the sole.

[D8] The dorsum over the hallux and toe 2 is smooth generic skin: no EHL cord onto the hallux, no extensor slip to toe 2. A lean 40-year-old's forefoot shows both as soft ridges catching the light; without them the forefoot reads as a mannequin's.

[D9] Toe 2's distal segment is finger-long, about 8 mm of bare skin between its DIP crease and the nail fold; a second toe's nail starts just past the crease, so the end of the toe is short and stubby.

[D10] The dorsal micro-relief is a single crackle that turns into crumpled-cellophane facets and glints wherever a highlight crosses it, the same on knuckle, shaft and web; real skin's lines are finer and softer, with pores and a duller, broken sheen.
[D11] A thin raised glossy arc still crosses the first MTP dorsum and notches the profile in the medial view; it reads as a healed bunion scar, where MTP skin shows a few fine, broken wrinkles.
[D12] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even groove across two-thirds of the toe, a knife cut, where real skin shows two or three short, soft, broken creases.

[D13] From below the hallux grows straight out of the ball with no toe-base sulcus and only a faint IP crease; a real big toe is set off from the ball pad by a deep curved crease, and both its pads bulge.
[D14] The hallux lunula has gone rather than been reshaped: the plate is one even pink to the fold, no dull half-moon and no depth to the bed, which adds to the painted-tile look.
[D15] The hallux nail's medial border kinks in an S halfway down where the fold pinches in, a crisp crooked gutter that reads as a mesh fault; a lateral fold rolls evenly along a smooth plate edge.

In clay the hallux is a smooth, inflated bulb: thin rims stand in for the nail folds, the pulp has no fat-pad lobing and the IP dorsum no knuckle rise, so the base mesh's softness shows under the added detail.
[D16] In the medial zoom the hallux plate goes near-white with soft vertical combing, like polished acrylic; keratin keeps a pink, translucent body with a smaller sheen broken by faint ridges.

[D17] At the lateral zoom the free edge is an opaque grey-green laminated strip of constant width with vertical striations, split from the plate by a thin red outline, its rounded corner melting into the fold skin.
[D18] Below the hallux free edge the pulp and hyponychium are soft and featureless while the side wall beside them carries a crisp crackle: detail sharp in one place and blurred in the next.
[D19] In the web zoom the shadowed recess dissolves into soft blotches with no micro-relief, like denoiser smear, so the web skin turns waxy where real skin keeps its fine lines at lower contrast.
[D20] In clay the hallux free edge sits over a crescent pocket with a rim concentric with the edge, as if the plate were set in a carved cup instead of meeting the hyponychium in a soft groove.
[D21] From below the hallux's nail corners and toe 2's free edge show past the pulps as dark slivers, and toe 2's tip ends in a crumpled outline; a pulp hides its nail from below.
